subject: Re: best way to emulate Rstudio's Compile Notebook at command line / in a makefile?

messages.author: 9a0033d9324fcea3
messages.subject: Re: best way to emulate Rstudio's Compile Notebook at command line / in a makefile?
parts:
Thanks to fellow workshop instructors, I will just answer my own question, in case anyone else wants to find this quickly. These sorts of commands seem to work.

Rscript -e "knitr::stitch(foo.R')"
Rscript -e "knitr::stitch_rmd(foo.R')"
Rscript -e "knitr::stitch_rhtml(foo.R')"

Am happy to be told there's other / better ways ....

On Sunday, May 19, 2013 7:17:33 AM UTC-7, Jennifer Bryan wrote:
Apologies if this is well-known or obvious to others. I am teaching a workshop and would love to include this and so far cannot find this info myself quickly.

Context: students have created a decent small R script that is self-contained and creates useful outputs. It is suitable for running via R CMD BATCH, for example.

We are showing how to use Makefile to structure an analytical pipeline that could include *.R files.

I'd like to achieve the same result as RStudio's File-->Compile Notebook but outside of RStudio. Doing a compare / contrast on having a pretty report that reflects what interactive execution would look like vs. explicitly writing all figs to file and using write, sink, etc. to write important facts to file.

What would I do at the command line to cause a self-contained script foo.R to be processed as if I had opened it in RStudio and done Compile Notebook?

With this useful information, I will use it in a Makefile sort of like so:

foo.html: data_needed_by_foo.txt foo.R
<R CMD BATCH foo.R>
but obviously my R CMD BATCH line is what I need to replace / upgrade for Compile Notebook functionality.

I've read about stitch() and spin() but just can't quite get this to come into focus and work :(

Thanks for any help,
Jenny

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: best way to emulate Rstudio's Compile Notebook at command line / in a makefile?
parts:
"Rscript -e" should be the best way to go. You can also write a shell
script (*nix) or batch file (Windows).

Regards,
